claim: Sam Altman: "AI will probably most likely lead to the end of the world, but in the meantime, there'll be great companies" (variant: "I think AI will probably, most likely, sort of lead to the end of the world. But in the meantime, there will be great companies created with serious machine learning.")

event.name: Airbnb Open Air 2015 conference: onstage interview with Sam Altman (then president of Y Combinator), prompted by Airbnb's Mike Curtis
event.date: Thursday. Most likely Thursday 4 June 2015 (inference, not stated in any source read): Business Insider says Altman spoke 'Thursday at Airbnb's Open Air 2015 conference'; the article is datelined June 4, 2015 (Yahoo Finance copy); 4 June 2015 was a Thursday. BI also says Thursday was the 10th anniversary of YC's investment in Altman's first company, Loopt.
event.place: not found. The Airbnb OpenAir page (http://nerds.airbnb.com/openair-tech-conference-2015/) returned a Cloudflare challenge and could not be read; a search snippet of it mentions CityView Metreon, June 8, but the page is headed 'Announcing OpenAir 2016', so it is unresolved and may not refer to this event. An Inc. article (search summary claimed it says 'Thursday in San Francisco') was behind a captcha and was not read.
event.curtis_title_note: Business Insider body: 'Mike Curtis, Airbnb's vice president of engineering'. BI/Yahoo photo caption: 'Airbnb CTO Mike Curtis'. TechRadar: 'then-Airbnb CTO Mike Curtis'. Sources conflict.

first_report.title: Head of Silicon Valley's most important startup farm says we're in a 'mega bubble' that won't last
first_report.author: Matt Weinberger
first_report.date: June 4, 2015 (Yahoo Finance copy dateline). Business Insider page timestamp: 2015-06-05T00:09:00.000Z.
syndicated_copies: https://malaysia.news.yahoo.com/head-silicon-valley-most-important-000927144.html (says 'Updated Fri, 5 June 2015 at 12:09 am UTC'; credits Business Insider)
first_report.exact_wording: AI will probably most likely lead to the end of the world, but in the meantime, there'll be great companies.
first_report.exact_context: Under the lead-in "Here are some of his thoughts:" the article gives: "On the growing artificial-intelligence market: 'AI will probably most likely lead to the end of the world, but in the meantime, there'll be great companies.'"
event_sentences_verbatim: According to Altman, speaking Thursday at Airbnb's Open Air 2015 conference, so much risk-free, low-interest capital is being lent by the US government that vast overinflation is present across the board...

Altman, with the prompting of Mike Curtis, Airbnb's vice president of engineering, in an onstage interview was on fire. He had thoughts on everything from how the world is going to end to why people would rather live next to a coal plant than a nuclear power plant.
caveats: The quote is a bullet in a reporter's summary, not a labelled verbatim transcript. The article does not contain 'I think' or 'like' or 'sort of' or 'machine learning'.
Business Insider page is partly paywalled ('available exclusively to Business Insider subscribers'), but the fetched HTML contained the full body including the quote.
No earlier report than June 4, 2015 was found in several searches.
